```{css, echo = FALSE}
table.dataTable { font-size: 0.85rem; }
table.dataTable thead th { vertical-align: bottom; }
table.dataTable td.cell-nowrap { white-space: nowrap; }
```

This document reproduces every table and figure of the paper from the saved results in `results/fair/`. It renders offline, at no cost, in a few minutes. It needs the images in `imgs/` (see the README). The switches in @sec-switches re-run the steps that call a paid API or need a GPU, and @sec-rerun lists all steps.

The study asks if structured decision models (JEV and Clef-Flash) can detect manufacturing defects as well as few-shot CLIP [@radford2021clip; @megahed2026clip], with fewer images in the prompt, and give calibrated probabilities. A structured decision model returns a probability for each allowed answer to a question about an image. In this design, every method gets the same labeled images, every method is calibrated on the same calibration images, and every comparison is paired on the same test images. @sec-v001 tells what changed from the first version, v0.0.1.

The runs of the decision models (the description loops, and the calibration and test runs) come after this version of the document. Task 10 of the plan `replication_materials/plans/2026-10-20-fair-comparison-plan.md` makes them. Until then, the sections that need them show a note, and they show the CLIP results that exist.

## Figure and table style

Figures use `theme_bw()` with the Dark2 palette, Outfit for titles and Cabin for all other text (both under the SIL Open Font License, in `fonts/`). Colored words in the subtitle replace the legend. Each figure is saved as PNG (600 dpi), PDF and SVG, in a one-column size (3.4 in wide) and a two-column size (7 in wide) for a two-column letter page. PDF and SVG files hold the text as outlines, so they look the same on every computer. Each table is saved as CSV and LaTeX and shown here as an interactive table.

```{r}
#| label: fonts-and-colors
# Fonts: register the files in fonts/ for ragg (PNG) and showtext (PDF, SVG).
title_font <- "Outfit"
body_font <- "Cabin"
fonts <- list(
  Outfit = c(plain = "fonts/Outfit-SemiBold.ttf", bold = "fonts/Outfit-Bold.ttf",
             italic = "fonts/Outfit-SemiBold.ttf"),
  Cabin = c(plain = "fonts/Cabin-Regular.ttf", bold = "fonts/Cabin-Bold.ttf",
            italic = "fonts/Cabin-Italic.ttf")
)
known <- c(systemfonts::system_fonts()$family,
           systemfonts::registry_fonts()$family)
purrr::iwalk(fonts, \(f, family) {
  if (!family %in% known) {
    systemfonts::register_font(family, plain = f[["plain"]], bold = f[["bold"]],
                               italic = f[["italic"]], bolditalic = f[["bold"]])
  }
  sysfonts::font_add(family, regular = f[["plain"]], bold = f[["bold"]],
                     italic = f[["italic"]], bolditalic = f[["bold"]])
})

# Colors: one per model, class and calibration method.
dark2 <- RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(8, "Dark2")
model_colors <- c("JEV" = dark2[1], "Clef-Flash" = dark2[3], "CLIP" = dark2[2])
class_colors <- c(nominal = "grey30", defective = dark2[4])
calibration_colors <- c(raw = "grey45", Platt = dark2[7], isotonic = dark2[5])
# Text in tables: 25% darker model colors. The Dark2 colors are below the
# WCAG AA contrast of 4.5:1 for text (JEV: 3.4:1 on white); the darker ones
# reach 5.1:1 or more on both table backgrounds.
model_text_colors <- purrr::map_chr(model_colors, \(color) {
  grDevices::rgb(t(grDevices::col2rgb(color) * 0.75), maxColorValue = 255)
})
# Background of every second dataset in the tables.
group_color <- "#F4F4F4"

# Markdown for a bold word in a color (ggtext), and the same in HTML (tables).
paint <- function(text, color) {
  as.character(stringr::str_glue("<span style='color:{color}'>**{text}**</span>"))
}
paint_html <- function(text, color) {
  as.character(stringr::str_glue("<span style='color:{color}'><b>{text}</b></span>"))
}

# Round half up, as in the paper. Floating point stores 0.725 as
# 0.72499..., so round() and sprintf() give 0.72.
round_half_up <- function(x, digits = 2) {
  sign(x) * floor(abs(x) * 10^digits + 0.5 + 1e-9) / 10^digits
}
# Fixed decimals; "+ 0" turns a rounded -0 into 0, so no "-0.00".
fmt <- function(x, digits = 2) {
  formatC(round_half_up(x, digits) + 0, format = "f", digits = digits)
}
signed <- function(x, digits = 2) {
  shown <- round_half_up(x, digits) + 0
  stringr::str_c(dplyr::if_else(shown < 0, "-", "+"), fmt(abs(shown), digits))
}
capitalize <- function(s) {
  stringr::str_c(stringr::str_to_upper(stringr::str_sub(s, 1, 1)),
                 stringr::str_sub(s, 2))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: figure-helpers
# Figure sizes for a two-column letter page.
layouts <- list(
  "one-column" = list(width = 3.4, base_size = 8),
  "two-column" = list(width = 7.0, base_size = 9)
)

# Titles: wrap at a fixed number of characters per layout.
headline <- function(text, layout) {
  width <- c("one-column" = 46, "two-column" = 84)[[layout]]
  stringr::str_wrap(text, width = width) |>
    stringr::str_replace_all("\n", "<br>")
}

# Subtitles are wrapped here, not by ggtext: its text boxes sometimes
# reserve one line less than they draw, and the subtitle then overlaps the
# title. Line length counts visible characters only, and a colored span
# never breaks across lines (its spaces become no-break spaces first).
subline <- function(layout, ...) {
  nbsp <- " "
  text <- stringr::str_c(...) |>
    stringr::str_replace_all("<span[^>]*>.*?</span>",
                             \(s) stringr::str_replace_all(s, " ", nbsp))
  words <- stringr::str_split_1(text, " ")
  visible <- stringr::str_length(stringr::str_remove_all(words, "<[^>]+>|\\*\\*"))
  width <- c("one-column" = 68, "two-column" = 125)[[layout]]
  lines <- character()
  current <- integer()
  for (i in seq_along(words)) {
    line_length <- sum(visible[current]) + length(current) + visible[i]
    if (length(current) > 0 && line_length > width) {
      lines <- c(lines, stringr::str_c(words[current], collapse = " "))
      current <- integer()
    }
    current <- c(current, i)
  }
  lines <- c(lines, stringr::str_c(words[current], collapse = " "))
  stringr::str_c(lines, collapse = "<br>") |>
    stringr::str_replace_all(nbsp, " ")
}

# The theme of all figures.
theme_paper <- function(layout) {
  ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = layouts[[layout]]$base_size,
                    base_family = body_font) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      plot.title = ggtext::element_markdown(
        family = title_font, face = "bold", lineheight = 1.1,
        size = ggplot2::rel(1.2), margin = ggplot2::margin(0, 0, 3, 0)
      ),
      plot.subtitle = ggtext::element_markdown(
        colour = "grey25", lineheight = 1.15,
        margin = ggplot2::margin(0, 0, 6, 0)
      ),
      plot.caption.position = "plot",
      plot.caption = ggtext::element_markdown(
        colour = "grey35", size = ggplot2::rel(0.8), hjust = 0,
        lineheight = 1.1, margin = ggplot2::margin(6, 0, 0, 0)
      ),
      panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      strip.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "grey95",
                                               colour = "grey70"),
      strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", colour = "grey20"),
      axis.title = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "grey25")
    )
}

# Save one figure in both sizes and three formats; show the two-column one.
save_figure <- function(make_plot, name, height) {
  purrr::iwalk(layouts, \(spec, layout) {
    plot <- make_plot(layout)
    dir.create(file.path(figs_dir, layout), recursive = TRUE,
               showWarnings = FALSE)
    stem <- file.path(figs_dir, layout, name)
    # PNG with ragg (system text rendering).
    ragg::agg_png(stringr::str_c(stem, ".png"), width = spec$width,
                  height = height[[layout]], units = "in", res = 600)
    print(plot)
    grDevices::dev.off()
    # PDF and SVG with showtext (text as outlines).
    devices <- list(pdf = grDevices::cairo_pdf, svg = grDevices::svg)
    purrr::iwalk(devices, \(open, extension) {
      open(stringr::str_c(stem, ".", extension), width = spec$width,
           height = height[[layout]])
      showtext::showtext_begin()
      print(plot)
      showtext::showtext_end()
      grDevices::dev.off()
    })
  })
  make_plot("two-column")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: table-helpers
# Save one table as CSV and LaTeX (for the paper) and show it as an
# interactive table. `widths` sets LaTeX column widths, `wide` names the
# long-text columns (the only ones that wrap), `filter` adds a filter box
# above each column, `display` (optional) is an HTML version of the table to
# show instead, `page_length` is the number of rows on one page, and `group`
# names a column (for example Dataset): all rows of one group share one
# background, which alternates between groups, in place of DT's stripe per
# row.
save_table <- function(data, name, caption, digits = 2, widths = NULL,
                       wide = NULL, filter = FALSE, display = NULL,
                       page_length = 15, group = NULL) {
  data <- dplyr::mutate(
    data,
    dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.double), \(v) round_half_up(v, digits))
  )

  # Files for the paper.
  dir.create(tables_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  readr::write_csv(data, file.path(tables_dir, stringr::str_c(name, ".csv")))
  latex <- kableExtra::kbl(data, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE,
                           caption = caption)
  for (column in names(widths)) {
    latex <- kableExtra::column_spec(latex, match(column, names(data)),
                                     width = widths[[column]])
  }
  writeLines(latex, file.path(tables_dir, stringr::str_c(name, ".tex")))

  # Interactive table: search and pages only for long tables.
  shown <- if (is.null(display)) data else display
  long <- nrow(shown) > page_length
  # unname(): a named vector would become a JSON object, which DT ignores.
  is_number <- unname(purrr::map_lgl(shown, is.numeric))
  is_wide <- names(shown) %in% wide
  column_defs <- list(
    list(className = "dt-left cell-nowrap", targets = which(!is_number & !is_wide) - 1),
    list(className = "dt-left", targets = which(!is_number & is_wide) - 1),
    list(className = "dt-right cell-nowrap", targets = which(is_number) - 1)
  )
  if (!is.null(wide)) {
    column_defs <- c(column_defs, list(list(
      width = if (length(wide) == 1) "35%" else "220px",
      targets = which(is_wide) - 1
    )))
  }
  widget <- DT::datatable(
    shown,
    escape = is.null(display), # the display version holds HTML
    rownames = FALSE,
    filter = if (filter) "top" else "none",
    class = if (is.null(group)) "compact stripe hover" else "compact hover",
    options = list(
      dom = if (long) "ftip" else "t",
      pageLength = page_length,
      scrollX = TRUE,
      autoWidth = !is.null(wide),
      columnDefs = column_defs
    )
  )
  # Fixed decimals for numbers; none for columns of whole numbers.
  doubles <- purrr::map_lgl(shown, is.double)
  whole <- purrr::map_lgl(shown, \(v) is.double(v) && all(v == round(v), na.rm = TRUE))
  if (any(doubles & !whole)) {
    widget <- DT::formatRound(widget, names(shown)[doubles & !whole], digits)
  }
  if (any(whole)) {
    widget <- DT::formatRound(widget, names(shown)[whole], digits = 0)
  }
  # One background per group, alternating between groups (white, light grey).
  if (!is.null(group)) {
    groups <- unique(shown[[group]])
    shades <- rep(c("#FFFFFF", group_color), length.out = length(groups))
    widget <- DT::formatStyle(widget, group, target = "row",
                              backgroundColor = DT::styleEqual(groups, shades))
  }
  widget
}
```

```{r}
test_set <- dplyr::filter(manifest, split == "test")

# Summaries of scripts/fair_evaluate.R. Before the decision-model runs they

scores_dir <- file.path(results_root, "scores")
summary_dir <- file.path(results_root, "summary")
metrics <- read_csv_quiet(file.path(summary_dir, "metrics.csv"))
paired <- read_csv_quiet(
  file.path(summary_dir, "paired.csv"),
  col_types = readr::cols(.default = "d", comparison = "c", model = "c",
                          dataset = "c", metric = "c")
)

# Closed loop logs and their audits (scripts/fair_close_loop.R). The mirror
# that the loop writes while it runs (<model>-<dataset>_loop_log.csv) does
# not count: only a closed loop has a _log.csv file.
loop_dir <- file.path(saved_root, "loop")
descriptions_dir <- file.path(saved_root, "descriptions")
read_loop_files <- function(kind) {
  pattern <- stringr::str_c("^(jev|clef)-(", stringr::str_c(dataset_order, collapse = "|"),
                            ")_", kind, "\\.csv$")
  files <- list.files(loop_dir, pattern = pattern, full.names = TRUE)
  if (length(files) == 0) {
    return(tibble::tibble(file = character(), model = character(), dataset = character()))
  }
  files |>
    rlang::set_names(basename(files)) |>
    purrr::map(\(f) read_csv_quiet(f, col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c"))) |>
    purrr::list_rbind(names_to = "file") |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      model = stringr::str_extract(file, "^[a-z]+"),
      dataset = stringr::str_match(file, stringr::str_c("^[a-z]+-(.+)_", kind))[, 2]
    )
}
loops <- read_loop_files("log")

if (nrow(loops) > 0) {
  loops <- dplyr::mutate(loops, candidate = as.integer(candidate),
                         auc = as.numeric(auc), kept = as.logical(kept))
}

# What exists decides which sections run. The guards look at the rows, not
# at the files: metrics.csv already exists with CLIP rows.
has_decision <- any(metrics$model %in% c("jev", "clef"))
has_loop <- nrow(loops) > 0
has_paired <- nrow(paired) > 0
has_comparison <- function(id) any(paired$comparison == id)
placeholder <- "Results appear after the runs of Task 10."

# A note in place of a section, or of its decision-model part.
note <- function(show, text = "") {
  if (show) {
    cat("\n::: {.callout-note}\n", placeholder, " ", text, "\n:::\n\n", sep = "")
  }
}

# Table of what exists now.
```

# Data

## Sets

The five datasets of @megahed2026clip are copies of [fmegahed/qe_genai/data](https://github.com/fmegahed/qe_genai/tree/main/data) in `imgs/`. The pipe staple images are from AutoVI [@carvalho2024autovi]. `results/image_split_manifest.csv` lists every image and its split. Before v0.0.1, duplicate pan test files and three extrusion frames that copied test frames were removed (README, section Data). `scripts/fair_draw_sets.R` draws the sets of the fair comparison from the non-test images of each dataset:

- **Learning set L.** The CLIP baseline set of each dataset: 50 images per class (pans: 10). The defective images are spread evenly over the defect types. The references and the design images come from L.
- **References.** k images per class from L, with k = 1, 2 or 4. The sets are nested: the references at k = 1 are in the set at k = 2, which is in the set at k = 4.
- **Design images.** The images of L that are not references at k = 2. The description loop scores its candidates on them.
- **Calibration set C.** 25 images per class from the non-test images that are not in L. The defective images are stratified over the defect types. Pans have no C, because all 20 non-test pan images are in L.
- **Test set.** The test sets of v0.0.1 and of the CLIP study. Each configuration scores the test set once.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sets
#| tbl-cap: "Datasets and sets (images, nominal + defective). Pans have no calibration set C: they calibrate on the images of L that are not references."
# Defect types of each dataset, from all its images, with readable names for
# three datasets.
named_types <- c(
  microstructure = "Band, Bimodal, SingleCrystal (low, medium, high)",
  pan_images = "One defective class",
  pipe_staple = "Missing staple"
)
defect_types <- manifest |>
  dplyr::filter(actual_class == "defective") |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_types = dplyr::n_distinct(defect_type),
    types = stringr::str_c(sort(unique(stringr::str_replace_all(defect_type, "_", " "))),
                           collapse = ", "),
    .by = dataset
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    types = dplyr::coalesce(unname(named_types[dataset]), types),
    types = dplyr::if_else(n_types > 1, stringr::str_c(n_types, " types: ", types), types)
  )

# "nominal + defective" counts of one set.
count_set <- function(data, name) {
  data |>
    dplyr::count(dataset, actual_class) |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = actual_class, values_from = n) |>
    dplyr::transmute(dataset, "{name}" := stringr::str_c(nominal, " + ", defective))
}

# Table T1.
t1 <- tibble::tibble(dataset = dataset_order) |>
  dplyr::left_join(defect_types, by = "dataset") |>
  dplyr::left_join(count_set(sets$learning, "learning"), by = "dataset") |>
  dplyr::left_join(count_set(sets$references, "references"), by = "dataset") |>
  dplyr::left_join(count_set(sets$design, "design"), by = "dataset") |>
  dplyr::left_join(count_set(sets$calibration, "calibration"), by = "dataset") |>
  dplyr::left_join(count_set(test_set, "test"), by = "dataset") |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Dataset = dataset_labels[dataset],
    `Defect types` = types,
    `Learning set L` = learning,
    `References in L (k = 4)` = references,
    `Design images` = dplyr::coalesce(design, "none (no loop)"),
    `Calibration set C` = dplyr::coalesce(calibration, "none"),
    `Test set` = test
  )
save_table(t1, "T1_sets", "Datasets and sets (images, nominal + defective).",
           wide = "Defect types", group = "Dataset")
```

## Label budget

The paper separates two numbers. The first is the number of images that the model sees for each test image: k per class. The second is the number of labeled images that the method needs in total. @tbl-budget gives the second number for each method, per class. JEV, Clef-Flash and the CLIP baseline need the same labeled images.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-budget
#| tbl-cap: "Label budget: labeled images per class that each method needs (k = 2). Pans have no C: JEV, Clef-Flash and CLIP with the same references calibrate on the images of L that are not references, the CLIP baseline on leave-one-out scores in L, and CLIP zero-shot on all of L."
# Images per class in L and in C (C: 0 for pans).
per_class <- function(data, name) {
  data |>
    dplyr::count(dataset, actual_class) |>
    dplyr::summarise("{name}" := min(n), .by = dataset)
}
k_main <- 2
budget <- tibble::tibble(dataset = dataset_order) |>
  dplyr::left_join(per_class(sets$learning, "n_l"), by = "dataset") |>
  dplyr::left_join(per_class(sets$calibration, "n_c"), by = "dataset") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    n_c = dplyr::coalesce(n_c, 0L),
    pans = dataset == "pan_images",
    decision = dplyr::if_else(pans, n_l, n_l + n_c),
    refs = dplyr::if_else(pans, n_l, k_main + n_c),
    zero = dplyr::if_else(pans, n_l, n_c)
  )

# Table T2: one row per method, one column per dataset.
t2 <- budget |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    dataset = dataset_labels[dataset],
    `JEV and Clef-Flash` = decision, `CLIP baseline` = decision,
    `CLIP, same references` = refs, `CLIP, zero-shot` = zero
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-dataset, names_to = "Method") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = dataset, values_from = value) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Learning = c("L (k references; the rest chooses the description)", "L",
                 "the k references", "none"),
    Calibration = "C",
    `Images seen per test image, per class` = c("k", "50 (pans 10)", "k", "0"),
    .after = Method
  )
save_table(t2, "T2_label_budget",
           "Label budget: labeled images per class that each method needs (k = 2).",
           digits = 0)
```

## Calibration draw

```{r}
#| label: draw-numbers
# Numbers for the text below.
draw <- sets$draw_report
excluded <- \(ds, class) draw$excluded_near_copies[draw$dataset == ds & draw$actual_class == class]
```

C excludes the near-copies of L and test images. CLIP scores an image by its highest similarity to the images of L. A C image that nearly copies an L image thus gets a very confident score, and a Platt fit on C becomes too steep for CLIP. The rule depends on the dataset (@tbl-draw):

- Extrusion frames come from video, so a frame can nearly copy another frame. The draw excluded `r excluded("extrusion", "nominal")` nominal and `r excluded("extrusion", "defective")` defective frames with a dHash distance of 6 or less to an L or test frame. This is the check of `experiments/check_leakage.R`, with the same distance limit.
- The other datasets show one fixed scene, so dHash flags almost every pair of images. They exclude byte-identical copies (MD5) only. The draw found none.

Pipe staple has only 17 defective images outside L and the test set. C then takes 17 images per class, so it stays balanced. Open item O3 stays open: L is the CLIP baseline set of the CLIP paper, and some extrusion test frames can nearly copy L frames. The paper states this as a limitation of the CLIP baseline on extrusion.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-draw
#| tbl-cap: "Draw of the calibration set C (seed 202611): the near-copy rule of each dataset, the images left after the exclusion, the excluded near-copies, and the images drawn. Shortfall: 25 minus the images drawn."
rule_labels <- c(
  dhash6 = "dHash distance of 6 or less to an L or test image",
  md5 = "Byte-identical (MD5) copy of an L or test image"
)
# Table T3.
t3 <- draw |>
  dplyr::arrange(match(dataset, dataset_order), dplyr::desc(actual_class == "nominal")) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Dataset = dataset_labels[dataset],
    Class = actual_class,
    `Near-copy rule` = unname(rule_labels[rule]),
    `Images left after exclusion` = available,
    `Excluded near-copies` = excluded_near_copies,
    Drawn = drawn,
    Shortfall = shortfall
  )
save_table(t3, "T3_calibration_draw", "Draw of the calibration set C (seed 202611).",
           digits = 0, wide = "Near-copy rule", group = "Dataset")
```

## Reference images

```{r}
#| label: fig-references
#| fig-cap: "The reference images at k = 2, the main setting. All come from the learning set L. Pipe staple images: AutoVI [@carvalho2024autovi], CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; other images: the data of @megahed2026clip."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 7.4
# Label of one reference image: its class, or its defect type.
type_names <- c(defective = "Defective", missing = "Missing staple",
                over = "Over-extrusion", under = "Under-extrusion",
                local = "Local defect", global = "Global defect")
tile_label <- function(class, type) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    class == "nominal" ~ "Nominal",
    type %in% names(type_names) ~ type_names[type],
    .default = capitalize(stringr::str_replace_all(type, "_", " "))
  )
}

# One image tile: center-cropped and scaled as sent to the models. The
# pixels go in as a numeric array; as.raster() of a magick image sometimes
# drew blank or garbled tiles.
tile_plot <- function(path, class, type, layout) {
  image <- magick::image_read(path)
  info <- magick::image_info(image)
  side <- min(info$width, info$height)
  pixels <- image |>
    magick::image_crop(stringr::str_glue("{side}x{side}"), gravity = "center") |>
    magick::image_scale("320x320!") |>
    magick::image_data(channels = "rgb") |>
    as.integer() # height x width x 3
  label <- tile_label(class, type)
  if (layout == "one-column") label <- stringr::str_replace(label, " ", "<br>")
  ggplot2::ggplot() +
    ggplot2::annotation_raster(pixels / 255, 0, 1, 0, 1) +
    ggplot2::coord_fixed(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), expand = FALSE) +
    ggplot2::labs(title = paint(label, class_colors[[class]])) +
    ggplot2::theme_void(base_size = layouts[[layout]]$base_size,
                        base_family = body_font) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      plot.title = ggtext::element_markdown(
        hjust = 0.5, size = ggplot2::rel(0.85), lineheight = 1.1,
        margin = ggplot2::margin(0, 0, 2, 0)
      ),
      plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(2, 2, 2, 2)
    )
}

# Dataset name at the start of each row.
row_label <- function(text, layout) {
  ggplot2::ggplot() +
    ggplot2::annotate(
      "text", x = 0, y = 0.5, label = text, hjust = 0, family = title_font,
      lineheight = 0.95, fontface = "bold",
      size = layouts[[layout]]$base_size / ggplot2::.pt
    ) +
    ggplot2::xlim(0, 1) +
    ggplot2::ylim(0, 1) +
    ggplot2::theme_void()
}

# Figure F1: one row per dataset, nominal images first.
refs_main <- dplyr::filter(sets$references, rank <= k_main)
fig_references <- function(layout) {
  tiles <- purrr::map(dataset_order, function(ds) {
    refs <- refs_main |>
      dplyr::filter(dataset == ds) |>
      dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(actual_class == "nominal"), rank)
    row <- purrr::pmap(
      list(refs$image_path, refs$actual_class, refs$defect_type),
      \(path, class, type) tile_plot(path, class, type, layout)
    )
    name <- if (layout == "one-column") short_labels[[ds]] else dataset_labels[[ds]]
    c(list(row_label(name, layout)), row)
  })
  patchwork::wrap_plots(unlist(tiles, recursive = FALSE), ncol = 1 + 2 * k_main,
                        widths = c(1.1, rep(1, 2 * k_main))) +
    patchwork::plot_annotation(
      title = headline("Two images per class are all the decision models see", layout),
      subtitle = subline(
        layout,
        paint("Nominal", class_colors[["nominal"]]), " and ",
        paint("defective", class_colors[["defective"]]),
        " reference images at k = 2, drawn from the learning set (seed 202610) ",
        "and center-cropped as sent to the models. Small images are enlarged ",
        "here for display only."
      ),
      # Image sources. AutoVI is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: the pipe staple tiles of
      # this figure keep that license.
      caption = subline(
        layout,
        "Images: Megahed et al. (2026), github.com/fmegahed/qe_genai. ",
        "Pipe staple: AutoVI (Carvalho et al., 2024), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0."
      ),
      theme = theme_paper(layout)
    )
}
save_figure(fig_references, "F1_reference_images",
            height = c("one-column" = 5.2, "two-column" = 7.4))
```

# Methods {#sec-methods}

## Common settings

All methods do the binary task: nominal or defective. The event class of all metrics is defective. Each image is center-cropped to a square and scaled to at most 768 px, with no upscaling (the frozen v0.0.1 setting). The models are JEV `jev-1.13.0` on the TypeSafe API [@typesafe2026images], Clef-Flash [@cloudflare2026clefflash] on a local SGLang server, and CLIP ViT-L/14 [@radford2021clip] on a local GPU. The settings of each model are those of v0.0.1.

## References

Each call to JEV or Clef-Flash holds k reference images per class, then the image to classify. The main setting is k = 2, so a call holds 4 references. The reference curve uses k = 0, 1, 2 and 4. The nominal references are a random draw from the nominal images of L. The defective references take one image per defect type, in a random order of the types, until there are k images. Pans and pipe staple have one defect type and take a random draw. The seed is 202610. JEV, Clef-Flash and CLIP use the same references (@fig-references). Microstructure has 9 defect types, so at k = 2 its references show only 2 of them. This is the cost of few references, and the curve to k = 4 measures it.

## Description loop

A description is the pair of texts that tells the model what a nominal and a defective image look like. The loop looks for a better description, for JEV and for Clef-Flash separately, on the four datasets other than pans:

- The design images are the images of L that are not references at k = 2 (48 per class).
- The loop starts from the generic description of `classify_image()`. Nominal: "No visible manufacturing defects; the part appears conforming." Defective: "At least one visible manufacturing defect or anomaly."
- A candidate changes only the two texts. The references (k = 2), the image size and the crop do not change. Each dataset and model has at most 6 candidates, including the start.
- The score of a candidate is its ROC AUC [@hanley1982auc] on the design images. A candidate replaces the current best if its AUC is at least 0.02 higher. The final description is the last one kept.
- A fresh Claude Code agent runs the loop, one agent for each model. It works in a sandbox folder that holds only the design images (with neutral file names), their class and defect type, the four reference images, the generic description, the scoring command and the loop instructions (`scripts/fair_loop_instructions.md`). It cannot see the test images, C or any result.
- The loop is blind: the instructions carry no dataset knowledge from the researchers (decision D74). The researchers approve the instructions before the loop starts, and they do not edit a description during the loop.
- `scripts/fair_close_loop.R` audits the transcript of the agent. It flags every tool call outside the sandbox, then freezes the final description.

The design AUC of the final description is optimistic, because the loop chose on these images. Its AUC on C is not, because C chose nothing. Pans have no loop: 20 images cannot give references, design images and calibration images. JEV and Clef-Flash use the generic description on pans.

## Calibration and decision

Each configuration scores C once, and then the test set once. `scripts/fair_score.R` refuses a second run, and a test run before the calibration run. Platt scaling [@platt1999probabilistic], fitted on the C scores of the same configuration, gives the calibrated probability. It uses the smoothed targets of Platt, so a C that separates perfectly still gives a finite fit. The decision is defective when the calibrated probability is 0.5 or more. No method tunes a threshold. C is balanced, so this rule aims at balanced accuracy. Isotonic regression [@zadrozny2002transforming], fitted on C, is a sensitivity analysis (@sec-isotonic).

Pans have no C. JEV, Clef-Flash and CLIP with the same references calibrate on the images of L that are not references; these images choose nothing. The CLIP baseline calibrates on leave-one-out scores in L. Near-identical pan photos make these scores optimistic. CLIP zero-shot calibrates on all 20 images of L.

## CLIP variants

The CLIP score of an image with labeled images is the softmax of its two highest cosine similarities: to the nominal images and to the defective images [@megahed2026clip]. The zero-shot score is the softmax of the similarities to two text prompts, the prompts of v0.0.1. A raw score of 0.5 or more thus means that the image is closer to the defective class: this is the rule of the CLIP paper.

| Variant | Learning images | Calibration | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| CLIP baseline | L | Platt on C (pans: leave-one-out on L) | the benchmark |
| CLIP, same references | the k references of JEV, k = 1, 2, 4 | Platt on C | the same few images as JEV |
| CLIP, zero-shot | none (text prompts of v0.0.1) | Platt on C | no labeled images in the model |
| CLIP, zero-shot with the final descriptions | none (the final JEV descriptions as text prompts, cut at 77 tokens) | Platt on C | does a better description help CLIP too? |
| CLIP, paper rule | L | none (raw score at 0.5) | continuity with the CLIP paper |

: CLIP variants. The variant with the final descriptions runs after the loops.

## Configurations {#sec-configurations}

| Model | Description | k per class | Datasets |
|---|---|---|---|
| JEV | final description of the loop | 0, 1, 2, 4 | 4 (pans: generic) |
| JEV | generic | 0, 2 | 4 |
| Clef-Flash | final description of its loop | 0, 1, 2, 4 | 4 (pans: generic) |
| Clef-Flash | generic | 0, 2 | 4 |
| CLIP | the variants above | as above | 5 |

: Configurations. Pans have 4 JEV and 4 Clef-Flash configurations, because their only description is the generic one.

## Metrics

Each configuration reports these metrics on C and on the test set, with the yardstick package: accuracy, balanced accuracy, sensitivity (recall), specificity, precision, F1, the Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), ROC AUC, the Brier score and the log loss. The expected calibration error (ECE) uses 10 equal-width bins [@guo2017calibration]; yardstick has no ECE, so `R/evaluation.R` has a short function. The factor level `defective` comes first, so yardstick uses it as the event.

The headline metrics are balanced accuracy and MCC. Balanced accuracy does not depend on the prevalence. MCC uses all four cells of the confusion matrix. F1 and precision ignore true negatives, and they change when the other class is the event. All test sets are balanced, so accuracy equals balanced accuracy on the test sets; the tables show both. After calibration, the metrics on C are in sample (column `in_sample` of `metrics.csv`), so the tables of this document use the test set.

## Paired comparisons {#sec-paired-methods}

These comparisons were fixed before the test runs (decision D71). Each one applies to each dataset and to each decision model (JEV and Clef-Flash):

| ID | Comparison | Goal |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Decision model (final description, k = 2, calibrated) against the CLIP baseline (calibrated) | a fair comparison with CLIP |
| P2 | Final description against generic description, both at k = 2 | the description makes a difference |
| P3 | k = 2 against k = 0, both with the final description | only a few images are necessary |

: Paired comparisons. Pans have no P2, because they have no loop; their P3 uses the generic description.

A paired bootstrap over the test images, stratified by class (2,000 resamples, seed 202612), gives the difference and its 95% percentile interval for balanced accuracy, MCC and AUC. An exact McNemar test on the correctness of each image is a second check. The McNemar p-values are Holm-adjusted within each model, over 14 tests (P1 to P3 for 4 datasets, P1 and P3 for pans).

# Description loop

For each dataset and model, the loop log keeps every candidate: its texts, its design AUC, the mean score per defect type, the reason that the agent gave and the transcript of the agent. @sec-loop-candidates shows all candidates.

```{r}
#| label: loop-note
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
note(!has_loop)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-loop
#| tbl-cap: "Description loop: the candidates of each dataset and model, the design AUC of the generic and of the final description (optimistic: the loop chose on these images), and their AUC on C at k = 2 (not optimistic). Audit: tool calls of the agent outside the sandbox."
#| eval: !expr has_loop
# AUC on C of the generic and final descriptions at k = 2 (raw scores: Platt
# keeps the order, and the raw AUC is not in sample).
auc_on_c <- metrics |>
  dplyr::filter(model %in% c("jev", "clef"), split == "calibration",
                calibration == "raw", metric == "roc_auc", k == k_main) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    c_generic = value[description == "generic"][1],
    c_final = value[description == "final"][1],
    .by = c(model, dataset)
  )

# Audit result of each loop: the number of flagged tool calls.
audit_summary <- audits |>
  dplyr::summarise(flagged = sum(tool != "none"), .by = c(model, dataset))

# One row per model and dataset. The final description is the last kept one.
loop_summary <- loops |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    candidates = dplyr::n(),
    final = max(candidate[kept]),
    design_generic = auc[candidate == 1],
    design_final = auc[candidate == max(candidate[kept])],
    .by = c(model, dataset)
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(auc_on_c, by = c("model", "dataset")) |>
  dplyr::left_join(audit_summary, by = c("model", "dataset"))

# Table T4.
t4 <- loop_summary |>
  dplyr::arrange(match(dataset, dataset_order), match(model, names(model_labels))) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Dataset = dataset_labels[dataset],
    Model = model_labels[model],
    Candidates = candidates,
    `Final candidate` = final,
    `Design AUC, generic` = design_generic,
    `Design AUC, final` = design_final,
    `AUC on C, generic` = c_generic,
    `AUC on C, final` = c_final,
    `Audit: calls outside the sandbox` = flagged
  )
save_table(t4, "T4_description_loop", "Description loop: candidates and AUC.",
           digits = 3, group = "Dataset")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-loop
#| fig-cap: "Design AUC of each candidate of the description loop. The diamond is the AUC of the final description on C."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| eval: !expr has_loop
# The current best after each candidate (the AUC of the last kept one).
loop_steps <- loops |>
  dplyr::arrange(model, dataset, candidate) |>
  dplyr::mutate(best = dplyr::if_else(kept, auc, NA_real_)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(model, dataset) |>
  tidyr::fill(best, .direction = "down") |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = factor(model_labels[model], names(model_colors)),
                dataset = label_dataset(dataset))
loop_final <- loop_summary |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(c_final)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = factor(model_labels[model], names(model_colors)),
                dataset = label_dataset(dataset))

# Figure F2: one row per model, one column per dataset.
fig_loop <- function(layout) {
  d <- loop_steps
  f <- loop_final
  if (layout == "one-column") {
    levels(d$dataset) <- short_labels[dataset_order]
    levels(f$dataset) <- short_labels[dataset_order]
  }
  ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(candidate, auc, colour = model)) +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
    ggplot2::geom_step(ggplot2::aes(y = best), direction = "hv", linewidth = 0.6) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(shape = kept), size = 1.6, stroke = 0.6) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(data = f, ggplot2::aes(final, c_final), shape = 23,
                        fill = "white", size = 2, stroke = 0.7) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = model_colors) +
    ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 1)) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:6) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0.5, 1, 0.1)) +
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.7, 6.3), ylim = c(0.45, 1.02)) +
    ggplot2::facet_grid(rows = ggplot2::vars(model), cols = ggplot2::vars(dataset)) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = headline("Design AUC of the candidate descriptions", layout),
      subtitle = subline(
        layout,
        "Candidates of ", paint("JEV", model_colors[["JEV"]]), " and ",
        paint("Clef-Flash", model_colors[["Clef-Flash"]]),
        ". Filled: kept (AUC at least 0.02 above the current best); open: not ",
        "kept. The line follows the current best. Diamond: AUC of the final ",
        "description on C, which chose nothing."
      ),
      x = "Candidate (1 = generic description)", y = "ROC AUC"
    ) +
    theme_paper(layout)
}
save_figure(fig_loop, "F2_description_loop",
            height = c("one-column" = 4.2, "two-column" = 4.2))
```

# Main results

@tbl-main gives all metrics on the test set for the five methods of the main comparison. All use Platt scaling on C and the decision at 0.5. JEV and Clef-Flash use the final description of their loop at k = 2 (pans: the generic description). On this page, the chart column shows the balanced accuracy of each method on an axis from 0.4 to 1, with a dashed line at the CLIP baseline of the same dataset. The rows of one dataset thus form a dot chart. The glyphs compare each method with the CLIP baseline (★): ▲ at least 0.02 higher, ● within 0.02, ▼ at least 0.02 lower. Point at a glyph or a dot for the values.

```{r}

```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-main
#| tbl-cap: "Main results on the test sets: all metrics, after Platt scaling on C, decision at 0.5. Chart: balanced accuracy on an axis from 0.4 to 1 (dashed: CLIP baseline). Glyphs against the CLIP baseline (★): ▲ at least 0.02 higher, ● within 0.02, ▼ at least 0.02 lower."
# The five methods of the main comparison, with their mark in the chart.
main_methods <- tibble::tribble(
  ~method,                        ~model, ~description, ~k, ~mark,
  "JEV, k = 2",                   "jev",  "final",      2,  "circle",
  "Clef-Flash, k = 2",            "clef", "final",      2,  "circle",
  "CLIP baseline",                "clip", "baseline",   50, "triangle",
  "CLIP, same references, k = 2", "clip", "refs",       2,  "diamond",
  "CLIP, zero-shot",              "clip", "zero",       0,  "open"
)
benchmark <- "CLIP baseline"
# The configuration of each method on each dataset. Pans: the decision
# models use the generic description, and the CLIP baseline has k = 10.
main_configs <- tidyr::expand_grid(main_methods, dataset = dataset_order) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    description = dplyr::if_else(model != "clip" & dataset == "pan_images",
                                 "generic", description),
    k = dplyr::if_else(description == "baseline" & dataset == "pan_images", 10, k)
  )

# Test metrics of one calibration ("platt", "raw" or "isotonic"), one row per
# configuration and dataset, one column per metric.
test_metrics <- function(cal) {
  metrics |>
    dplyr::filter(split == "test", calibration == cal) |>
    dplyr::select(model, description, k, dataset, metric, value) |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = metric, values_from = value)
}
main <- main_configs |>
  dplyr::inner_join(test_metrics("platt"),
                    by = c("model", "description", "k", "dataset")) |>
  dplyr::arrange(match(dataset, dataset_order), match(method, main_methods$method))

# Table T5 (CSV and LaTeX: values only).
t5 <- main |>
  dplyr::transmute(Dataset = dataset_labels[dataset], Method = method,
                   dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(names(metric_labels)))) |>
  dplyr::rename_with(\(x) unname(metric_labels[x]), dplyr::all_of(names(metric_labels)))

# Interactive view, part 1: glyphs. Each method against the CLIP baseline on
# the same dataset (balanced accuracy as shown, margin 0.02).
glyph <- function(diff, tip) {
  up <- diff >= 0.02 - 1e-9
  down <- diff <= -0.02 + 1e-9
  color <- dplyr::case_when(up ~ "#1B7837", down ~ "#B2182B", .default = "#555555")
  symbol <- dplyr::case_when(up ~ "&#9650;", down ~ "&#9660;", .default = "&#9679;")
  as.character(stringr::str_glue("<span style='color:{color}' title='{tip}'>{symbol}</span>"))
}

# Interactive view, part 2: the chart cell of one row. Inline SVG with no
# script, so it works offline. Axis 0.4 to 1; grid at 0.5, 0.75 and 1.
svg_mark <- function(mark, cx, cy, color) {
  switch(mark,
    triangle = stringr::str_glue("<path d='M{cx},{cy - 5.5} l5.5,9.5 l-11,0 z' fill='{color}'/>"),
    diamond = stringr::str_glue("<path d='M{cx},{cy - 5.5} l5.5,5.5 l-5.5,5.5 l-5.5,-5.5 z' fill='{color}'/>"),
    open = stringr::str_glue("<circle cx='{cx}' cy='{cy}' r='4.3' fill='white' stroke='{color}' stroke-width='1.8'/>"),
    stringr::str_glue("<circle cx='{cx}' cy='{cy}' r='4.8' fill='{color}'/>")
  )
}
clip_color <- model_colors[["CLIP"]]
chart_cell <- function(ba, base, mark, color, tip) {
  x <- \(v) round(6 + (pmin(pmax(v, 0.4), 1) - 0.4) / 0.6 * 148, 1)
  ticks <- x(c(0.5, 0.75, 1))
  grid <- stringr::str_c(
    stringr::str_glue("<line x1='{ticks}' x2='{ticks}' y1='0' y2='20' stroke='#E5E5E5'/>"),
    collapse = ""
  )
  base_line <- stringr::str_glue(
    "<line x1='{x(base)}' x2='{x(base)}' y1='0' y2='20' stroke='{clip_color}' stroke-dasharray='3,2'/>"
  )
  as.character(stringr::str_glue(
    "<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' width='160' height='20' role='img' ",
    "aria-label='{tip}'><title>{tip}</title>{grid}{base_line}",
    "{svg_mark(mark, x(ba), 10, color)}</svg>"
  ))
}

# The display version of T5: chart and glyphs for balanced accuracy, method
# names in the darker text color of their model.
t5_display <- main |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    base_ba = bal_accuracy[method == benchmark],
    base_mcc = mcc[method == benchmark],
    .by = dataset
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    ba_diff = round_half_up(bal_accuracy, 3) - round_half_up(base_ba, 3),
    color = unname(model_colors[model_labels[model]]),
    tip = stringr::str_glue(
      "{method}: BA {fmt(bal_accuracy, 3)}, MCC {fmt(mcc, 3)}; ",
      "{signed(ba_diff, 3)} BA and ",
      "{signed(mcc - base_mcc, 3)} MCC against the CLIP baseline"
    ),
    chart = purrr::pmap_chr(list(bal_accuracy, base_ba, mark, color, tip), chart_cell),
    ba_cell = dplyr::if_else(
      method == benchmark,
      as.character(stringr::str_glue(
        "<span title='The CLIP baseline: the benchmark'>&#9733;</span> <b>{fmt(bal_accuracy, 3)}</b>"
      )),
      stringr::str_c(glyph(ba_diff, tip),
                     " ", fmt(bal_accuracy, 3))
    ),
    Method = paint_html(method, unname(model_text_colors[model_labels[model]]))
  ) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Dataset = dataset_labels[dataset], Method,
    `Chart: balanced accuracy, 0.4 to 1` = chart,
    `Balanced accuracy` = ba_cell,
    dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(setdiff(names(metric_labels), "bal_accuracy")))
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename_with(\(x) unname(metric_labels[x]),
                     dplyr::all_of(setdiff(names(metric_labels), "bal_accuracy")))
save_table(t5, "T5_main_results",
           "Main results on the test sets: all metrics, after Platt scaling on C.",
           digits = 3, display = t5_display, page_length = 25, group = "Dataset")
```

# Paired comparisons

The paired comparisons P1 to P3 (@sec-paired-methods) use the Platt probabilities and the decision at 0.5 on the same test images. Each figure shows the difference (decision model minus the other side) and its paired 95% bootstrap interval. An interval that does not cross 0 shows a difference that the test images support. The table at the end of this section adds the McNemar p-values, before and after the Holm adjustment.

```{r}
#| label: paired-note
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
note(!has_paired)
```

```{r}
#| label: paired-figure
#| eval: !expr has_paired
# Forest figure of one comparison: one row per dataset, one panel per
# headline metric, one point and interval per decision model.
headline_metrics <- c("bal_accuracy", "mcc", "roc_auc")
forest_data <- function(id) {
  d <- paired |>
    dplyr::filter(comparison == id) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      model = factor(model_labels[model], names(model_colors)),
      metric = factor(metric_labels[metric], metric_labels[headline_metrics])
    )
  present <- intersect(dataset_order, d$dataset)
  # Datasets top to bottom; JEV just above Clef-Flash in each row.
  dplyr::mutate(d, y = match(dataset, present) +
                  dplyr::if_else(model == "JEV", -0.15, 0.15))
}
fig_forest <- function(id, title, text) {
  d <- forest_data(id)
  present <- intersect(dataset_order, d$dataset)
  function(layout) {
    labels <- if (layout == "one-column") short_labels[present] else dataset_labels[present]
    ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(difference, y, colour = model)) +
      ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.3) +
      ggplot2::geom_linerange(ggplot2::aes(xmin = low, xmax = high), linewidth = 0.6) +
      ggplot2::geom_point(size = 1.8) +
      ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = model_colors) +
      ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq_along(present), labels = labels,
                                  transform = "reverse") +
      ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(metric), scales = "free_x",
                          ncol = if (layout == "one-column") 1 else 3) +
      ggplot2::labs(
        title = headline(title, layout),
        subtitle = subline(
          layout,
          "Difference and paired 95% bootstrap interval for ",
          paint("JEV", model_colors[["JEV"]]), " and ",
          paint("Clef-Flash", model_colors[["Clef-Flash"]]),
          " on the test images. ", text
        ),
        x = "Difference", y = NULL
      ) +
      theme_paper(layout) +
      ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.major.y = ggplot2::element_blank())
  }
}
forest_heights <- c("one-column" = 5.6, "two-column" = 3.2)
```

# Reference curve

@fig-reference-curve shows the test balanced accuracy and AUC against the number of references per class, k = 0, 1, 2 and 4. The decision models use the final description (pans: generic) at every k, so only the references change. For CLIP, k = 0 is zero-shot, and k > 0 uses the same references as the decision models. All values use Platt scaling on C. The bars give the paired 95% interval of the change from k = 0, placed at the value: a bar that does not reach the value at k = 0 shows a change that the test images support.

```{r}
#| label: curve-note
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
note(!has_decision, "Until then, the figure shows CLIP only.")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-reference-curve
#| fig-cap: "Test balanced accuracy and AUC against the number of references per class (Platt scaling on C). Bars: paired 95% interval of the change from k = 0."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 3.8
# Values and intervals; the interval of the change from k = 0 is moved to the
# value at k (value at k = 0 plus the bounds). Models side by side at each k.
curve <- k_curve |>
  dplyr::filter(metric %in% c("bal_accuracy", "roc_auc")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(k0 = value[k == 0], .by = c(model, dataset, metric)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    low_value = k0 + low, high_value = k0 + high,
    x = k + unname(c(jev = -0.12, clef = 0, clip = 0.12)[model]),
    model = factor(model_labels[model], names(model_colors)),
    metric = factor(metric_labels[metric], metric_labels[c("bal_accuracy", "roc_auc")]),
    dataset = label_dataset(dataset)
  )
curve_models <- intersect(names(model_colors), as.character(curve$model))

# Figure F6: metrics by dataset (two-column) or datasets by metric
# (one-column).
fig_curve <- function(layout) {
  d <- curve
  if (layout == "one-column") {
    levels(d$dataset) <- short_labels[dataset_order]
    facets <- ggplot2::facet_grid(rows = ggplot2::vars(dataset), cols = ggplot2::vars(metric))
  } else {
    facets <- ggplot2::facet_grid(rows = ggplot2::vars(metric), cols = ggplot2::vars(dataset))
  }
  model_text <- purrr::map_chr(curve_models, \(m) paint(m, model_colors[[m]]))
  ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, value, colour = model)) +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) +
    ggplot2::geom_linerange(ggplot2::aes(ymin = low_value, ymax = high_value),
                            linewidth = 0.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(size = 1.4) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = model_colors) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 1, 2, 4)) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0.4, 1, 0.2)) +
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.3, 1.02)) +
    facets +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = headline("Test results against the number of references per class", layout),
      subtitle = subline(
        layout,
        stringr::str_c(model_text, collapse = ", "),
        " after Platt scaling on C. CLIP at k = 0 is zero-shot. Bars: paired ",
        "95% interval of the change from k = 0, placed at the value."
      ),
      x = "References per class (k)", y = NULL
    ) +
    theme_paper(layout)
}
save_figure(fig_curve, "F6_reference_curve",
            height = c("one-column" = 6.4, "two-column" = 3.8))
```

# Calibration

Raw scores are not probabilities that a quality engineer can trust. @tbl-calibration gives the ECE, the Brier score and the log loss on the test set before (raw) and after Platt scaling on C. @fig-reliability shows the reliability diagrams of the decision models and of the CLIP baseline. The raw CLIP scores are the softmax of two cosine similarities, which differ little, so they stay near 0.5.

```{r}
#| label: calibration-note
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
note(!has_decision, "Until then, the table and the figure show CLIP only.")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-calibration
#| tbl-cap: "Calibration on the test sets: ECE, Brier score and log loss of the raw scores and after Platt scaling on C."
# Raw and Platt metrics of the main methods.
calibration_rows <- c("raw", "platt") |>
  purrr::map(\(cal) dplyr::mutate(test_metrics(cal), calibration = cal)) |>
  purrr::list_rbind() |>
  dplyr::inner_join(main_configs, by = c("model", "description", "k", "dataset")) |>
  dplyr::select(method, dataset, calibration, ece, brier_class, mn_log_loss) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = calibration,
                     values_from = c(ece, brier_class, mn_log_loss)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(match(dataset, dataset_order), match(method, main_methods$method))

# Table T7.
t7 <- calibration_rows |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Dataset = dataset_labels[dataset], Method = method,
    `ECE raw` = ece_raw, `ECE Platt` = ece_platt,
    `Brier raw` = brier_class_raw, `Brier Platt` = brier_class_platt,

  )
save_table(t7, "T7_calibration", "Calibration on the test sets.", digits = 3,
           page_length = 25, group = "Dataset")

# The reliability figure below has one panel per method and dataset, for
# the two decision models and the CLIP baseline. Its height follows the
# number of panels (five per row; three in the one-column size).
reliability_methods <- c("JEV, k = 2", "Clef-Flash, k = 2", "CLIP baseline")
n_panels <- sum(calibration_rows$method %in% reliability_methods)
reliability_heights <- c(
  "one-column" = 1.5 + 1.5 * ceiling(n_panels / 3),
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-reliability
#| fig-cap: "Reliability diagrams on the test sets: observed defect rate against the mean probability in 10 equal bins, for the raw scores and after Platt scaling on C."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: !expr reliability_heights[["two-column"]]
# Calibrated probabilities of every image, from the score files (the same
# fits as scripts/fair_evaluate.R).
calibrated <- list.files(scores_dir, pattern = "^(jev|clef|clip)_.+_(calibration|test)\\.csv$",
                         full.names = TRUE) |>
  purrr::map(read_csv_quiet) |>
  purrr::list_rbind() |>
  fair$calibrate_all()

# Test probabilities of the two decision models and the CLIP baseline, in
# 10 equal bins.
reliability <- main_configs |>
  dplyr::filter(method %in% reliability_methods) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::filter(calibrated, split == "test"),
                    by = c("model", "description", "k", "dataset")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(raw, platt), names_to = "calibration", values_to = "p") |>
  dplyr::mutate(bin = cut(p, seq(0, 1, 0.1), include.lowest = TRUE),
                y = as.integer(actual_class == "defective")) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mean_p = mean(p), observed = mean(y), n = dplyr::n(),
                   .by = c(method, dataset, calibration, bin)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(method, dataset, calibration, mean_p) |>
  dplyr::mutate(calibration = factor(dplyr::if_else(calibration == "platt", "Platt", "raw"),
                                     names(calibration_colors)))

# Strip of each panel: dataset, method, and the test ECE before and after
# Platt in their colors. Panels go by method, then by dataset.
strip_text <- function(layout) {
  labels <- if (layout == "one-column") {
    stringr::str_replace(short_labels, "\n", "<br>")
  } else {
    dataset_labels
  }
  calibration_rows |>
    dplyr::filter(method %in% reliability_methods) |>
    dplyr::arrange(match(method, reliability_methods), match(dataset, dataset_order)) |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      method, dataset,
      strip = stringr::str_c(
        "**", labels[dataset], "**<br>", method, "<br>ECE ",
        paint(fmt(ece_raw), calibration_colors[["raw"]]), " to ",
        paint(fmt(ece_platt), calibration_colors[["Platt"]])
      ),
      strip = factor(strip, strip)
    )
}

# Figure F7: five panels per row (two-column) or three (one-column).
fig_reliability <- function(layout) {
  d <- dplyr::inner_join(reliability, strip_text(layout), by = c("method", "dataset"))
  ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(mean_p, observed, colour = calibration)) +
    ggplot2::geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.55) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(size = 0.9) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = calibration_colors) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(strip), ncol = if (layout == "one-column") 3 else 5) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = headline("Reliability of the test probabilities before and after Platt scaling", layout),
      subtitle = subline(
        layout,
        paint("Raw", calibration_colors[["raw"]]), " scores and ",
        paint("Platt", calibration_colors[["Platt"]]),
        " probabilities, fitted on C. Calibrated curves follow the diagonal. ",
        "Strips give the test ECE before and after Platt scaling."
      ),
      x = "Mean predicted defect probability (10 bins)",
      y = "Observed defect rate"
    ) +
    theme_paper(layout) +
    ggplot2::theme(strip.text = ggtext::element_markdown(face = "plain", lineheight = 1.2))
}
save_figure(fig_reliability, "F7_reliability", height = reliability_heights)
```

# v0.0.1 {#sec-v001}

Version v0.0.1 is the tag [`v0.0.1`](https://github.com/fmegahed/decision-models-for-industrial-image-qc/tree/v0.0.1) (commit 33ffd59). Its analysis document, tables and figures stay in the tag, and the v0.0.1 scripts in `scripts/` reproduce it. The v0.0.1 results stay in the replication record. A reader can find five weak points in v0.0.1:

1. The calibration used the validation images that chose the description. A description that separates these images well looks better on them than on new images. Thus the calibrated probabilities were too confident.
2. The label budgets were different: 103 to 104 labeled images for JEV, 100 for the CLIP baseline, and mostly different images.
3. Claude Code wrote the descriptions after it had seen test results.
4. Clef-Flash used a description that was optimized for JEV.
5. CLIP was not calibrated, and the report gave only two metrics.

| Item | v0.0.1 | This design |
|---|---|---|
| Labeled images, JEV and Clef-Flash | 3 to 4 references plus 100 validation images (pans: 4 + 16) | 50 per class for learning (the references come from it) plus 25 per class for calibration |
| Labeled images, CLIP baseline | 50 per class (pans: 10) | the same 75 per class as JEV |
| Same images for all methods | partly | yes |
| Description chosen on | the 100 validation images | the learning images that are not references (48 per class) |
| Description written by | Claude Code, which had seen test results | a fresh agent that cannot see test images or results |
| Clef-Flash description | the description of JEV | its own loop |
| Threshold | tuned on raw validation probabilities | 0.5 on calibrated probabilities |
| Calibration fitted on | the validation images that chose the description | the separate calibration set C |
| CLIP calibrated | no | yes |
| Metrics | balanced accuracy and AUC | all metrics of @sec-methods, with paired comparisons |

: What changed from v0.0.1.

The v0.0.1 runs used the test sets once, and this design keeps the same test sets. A new test set would break the comparison with the CLIP paper, and pans have no spare images. Thus the researchers know the v0.0.1 test results, but the agent that writes the descriptions does not.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-isotonic
#| tbl-cap: "Sensitivity analysis: test results of every configuration after Platt scaling and after isotonic regression, both fitted on C. Use the boxes above the columns to filter."
# Readable name of a configuration.
config_label <- function(model, description, k) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    description == "baseline" ~ "CLIP baseline",
    description == "refs" ~ stringr::str_c("CLIP, same references, k = ", k),
    description == "zero" ~ "CLIP, zero-shot",
    description == "zero_final" ~ "CLIP, zero-shot, final descriptions",
    .default = stringr::str_c(model_labels[model], ", ", description,
                              " description, k = ", k)
  )
}
order_configs <- function(data) {
  dplyr::arrange(data, match(dataset, dataset_order),
                 match(model, names(model_labels)), description, k)
}

# Table A1: Platt against isotonic, every configuration.
a1 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(test_metrics("platt"), calibration = "Platt"),
  dplyr::mutate(test_metrics("isotonic"), calibration = "isotonic")
) |>
  dplyr::select(model, description, k, dataset, calibration, bal_accuracy, mcc,
                ece, mn_log_loss) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = calibration,
                     values_from = c(bal_accuracy, mcc, ece, mn_log_loss)) |>
  order_configs() |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Dataset = dataset_labels[dataset],
    Configuration = config_label(model, description, k),
    `BA Platt` = bal_accuracy_Platt, `BA isotonic` = bal_accuracy_isotonic,
    `MCC Platt` = mcc_Platt, `MCC isotonic` = mcc_isotonic,
    `ECE Platt` = ece_Platt, `ECE isotonic` = ece_isotonic,
    `Log loss Platt` = mn_log_loss_Platt, `Log loss isotonic` = mn_log_loss_isotonic
  )
save_table(a1, "A1_isotonic", "Test results after Platt scaling and after isotonic regression.",
           digits = 3, filter = TRUE, group = "Dataset")
```

## CLIP variants

The CLIP paper rule is the raw score of the CLIP baseline at 0.5. All other rows use Platt scaling on C.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-clip
#| tbl-cap: "All CLIP variants on the test sets. Use the boxes above the columns to filter."
# Table A3: the CLIP rows after Platt, plus the CLIP baseline with the rule of
# the CLIP paper (raw score at 0.5).
a3 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::filter(test_metrics("platt"), model == "clip"),
  test_metrics("raw") |>
    dplyr::filter(model == "clip", description == "baseline") |>
    dplyr::mutate(description = "paper_rule")
) |>
  order_configs() |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Dataset = dataset_labels[dataset],
    Variant = dplyr::if_else(description == "paper_rule", "CLIP baseline, paper rule",
                             config_label(model, description, k)),
    dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(names(metric_labels)))
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename_with(\(x) unname(metric_labels[x]), dplyr::all_of(names(metric_labels)))
save_table(a3, "A3_clip_variants", "All CLIP variants on the test sets.",
           digits = 3, filter = TRUE, group = "Dataset")
```

# Re-run steps {#sec-rerun}

These steps make all results of `results/fair/` from the images. Each step is a script in `scripts/`, run from the repository root. Steps marked **paid** call the TypeSafe API and need `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` in `.Renviron` (never commit it), a budget row in `replication_materials/calls/README.md`, and the call log `replication_materials/calls/typesafe-calls.csv`. The guards of `scripts/fair_score.R` stop a JEV run that needs more calls than the budget row has left; `JEV_CHECK_ONLY=true` runs the checks only. The original runs used the calls of the budget row, so a re-run of a paid step needs a new budget row first.

| Step | Script | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Draw L, C, the references and the design images | `Rscript scripts/fair_draw_sets.R` | none |
| 2. Score the CLIP variants | `RETICULATE_PYTHON=<env>/python.exe Rscript scripts/fair_clip.R` | local GPU |
| 3. Make the sandbox of a loop | `Rscript scripts/fair_make_sandbox.R <model> <dataset>` | none |
| 4. Run the loop | a fresh Claude Code agent in the sandbox reads `LOOP.md` and runs `score.sh`, which calls `scripts/fair_score.R` with `FAIR_SPLIT=design` | **paid** for JEV (up to 576 calls per dataset); local GPU for Clef-Flash |
| 5. Close the loop | `Rscript scripts/fair_close_loop.R <model> <dataset> <transcript>` | none |
| 6. Calibration and test runs | `FAIR_MODEL=<model> FAIR_DATASET=<dataset> FAIR_DESCRIPTION=<final or generic> FAIR_K=<k> FAIR_SPLIT=calibration Rscript scripts/fair_score.R`, then the same with `FAIR_SPLIT=test` | **paid** for JEV; local GPU for Clef-Flash |
| 7. Metrics, paired comparisons and k-curve | `Rscript scripts/fair_evaluate.R` | none |

: Re-run steps.

Notes on the steps:

- Step 1 rewrites `results/fair/sets/` with the same draws (the seeds are fixed). Check with `git diff` that the files do not change.
- Step 2 needs a Python 3.12 environment with torch 2.8.0 and OpenAI CLIP (`results/clip/python_environment.txt`). After the loops, `FAIR_CLIP_TEXT=final` adds the zero-shot variant with the final descriptions. Run CLIP when no other process uses the GPU.
- Steps 3 to 5 run once for each model (jev, clef) and dataset (extrusion, textiles, pipe_staple, microstructure). The researchers approve `LOOP.md` before step 4. Run the agent as a separate `claude -p` process with the sandbox as its working folder, so that it gets no project instructions and no project memory. Step 5 refuses to overwrite a frozen description.
- Step 6 runs the configurations of @sec-configurations. Clef-Flash needs its local server: `docker run --gpus all -p 30000:30000 lmsysorg/sglang:dev-clef sglang serve --model-path Cloudflare/clef-flash --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000`.
- `FAIR_OUT`, `FAIR_SCORES` and `FAIR_SUMMARY` send the outputs to another folder. The chunks below write to `results/rerun/fair/`, so the saved results never change. To build this document from the re-run outputs, set `results_root` to `rerun_root` in @sec-switches and render again.

The chunks below run only when their switch in @sec-switches is `TRUE`.

```{r}
#| label: rerun-helpers
# Run one script with environment variables and arguments; the old values
# of the variables come back after the run.
run_script <- function(script, vars = character(), args = character()) {
  status <- withr::with_envvar(vars, {
    system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"), c(script, args))
  })
  if (!identical(status, 0L)) {
    stop(script, " failed: ", stringr::str_c(names(vars), vars, sep = "=", collapse = " "))
  }
}

# The calibration and test runs of one decision model (section Configurations):
# all calibration runs first, then the test runs.
score_plan <- tidyr::expand_grid(dataset = dataset_order,
                                 description = c("final", "generic"),
                                 k = c(0, 1, 2, 4)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(description = dplyr::if_else(dataset == "pan_images", "generic",
                                             description)) |>
  dplyr::distinct() |>
  dplyr::filter(description == "final" | k %in% c(0, 2) | dataset == "pan_images")
rerun_scores <- function(model) {
  for (split in c("calibration", "test")) {
    purrr::pwalk(score_plan, \(dataset, description, k) {
      run_script("scripts/fair_score.R", c(
        FAIR_MODEL = model, FAIR_DATASET = dataset, FAIR_DESCRIPTION = description,
        FAIR_K = as.character(k), FAIR_SPLIT = split,
        FAIR_OUT = file.path(rerun_root, "scores")
      ))
    })
  }
}
```

```{r}
#| label: rerun-clip
#| eval: !expr run_clip
# Step 2: the CLIP variants, then the zero-shot variant with the final
# descriptions.
run_script("scripts/fair_clip.R", c(FAIR_OUT = file.path(rerun_root, "scores")))
run_script("scripts/fair_clip.R", c(FAIR_OUT = file.path(rerun_root, "scores"),
                                    FAIR_CLIP_TEXT = "final"))
```

```{r}
#| label: rerun-clef
#| eval: !expr run_clef
# Step 6 for Clef-Flash (local server at localhost:30000).
rerun_scores("clef")
```

```{r}
#| label: rerun-jev
#| eval: !expr run_jev
# Step 6 for JEV (paid; needs a budget row with enough calls left).
rerun_scores("jev")
```

```{r}
#| label: rerun-evaluate
#| eval: !expr run_evaluate
# Step 7: the summaries of the scores in results_root, written to rerun_root.
run_script("scripts/fair_evaluate.R", c(
  FAIR_SCORES = file.path(results_root, "scores"),
  FAIR_SUMMARY = file.path(rerun_root, "summary")
))
```
